scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the village of Nestani in Arkadia, Peloponnesus.
It is performed on the feast day of St. George, usually after Easter Sunday, to commemorate the protection of villagers from the Ottomans and to honor the Hagia Sophia.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed on the feast day of St. George, typically after Easter Sunday.
It serves to commemorate the protection of the villagers from the Ottomans and references the Hagia Sophia.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a line, with men leading and women following.
Men carry shepherd's crooks entwined with wildflowers and green leaves, held with the hand bent at the elbow.
The dance consists of ten basic steps divided into four parts.
Watch for Crook procession.
